affected_use.snippet:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $\mu$ be a $p$-restricted
partition of $d\ge1$; write $D(\mu)$ for the simple $kS_d$-module labelled by
$\mu$
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]],
[[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]).
Let $A_i$ denote the good $i$-node of $\mu$, for those
$i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$$\operatorname{soc}_{S_{d-1}}\bigl(D(\mu){\downarrow}_{S_{d-1}}\bigr)=\bigoplus_{i:\,\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0}D(\mu\setminus A_i),$$
a multiplicity-free sum over distinct simple modules: distinct residues give
distinct summands. The sum runs over the residues $i$ with
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$, one good node per such residue; the completely
reducible special case (the restriction is semisimple if and only if every
normal node is good, Kleshchev II Theorem 0.6) is a separate statement and is
not asserted here.

[F2] For a residue $i$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$ the good $i$-node $A_i$ is the unique normal $i$-node with no normal $i$-node above it, and the nodes $A_i$ for distinct residues $i$ are distinct nodes of $\mu$, so the partitions $\mu\setminus A_i$ of $d-1$ are distinct ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

affected_use.snippet:
On the set of $p$-restricted partitions
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]) define partial operators
$\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ for $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ by
$$\tilde e_i\mu:=\mu\setminus A\quad\text{if }\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0,$$
where $A$ is the good $i$-node of $\mu$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]), the
operator being undefined on $\mu$ when $\varepsilon_i(\mu)=0$; and
$$\tilde f_i\mu:=\mu\cup B\quad\text{if }\varphi_i(\mu)>0,$$
where $B$ is the cogood $i$-node of $\mu$, the operator being undefined on
$\mu$ when $\varphi_i(\mu)=0$. Then
$$\mu=\tilde f_i\nu\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\nu=\tilde e_i\mu$$
for all $p$-restricted $\mu,\nu$; in particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$
are mutual inverses on their domains, each $\tilde e_i$ lowers the rank by one
and each $\tilde f_i$ raises the rank by one, and at most one good and at most
one cogood node exist in each residue. No module-theoretic statement is made
here: this item is pure combinatorics, and the identification of these
operators with the crystal operators of the level-one Fock space is a theorem
of the later Fock-space page, not an input here.

[F1] For a $p$-restricted partition $\lambda$ the $i$-signature is the word in $\{+,-\}$ read off the addable and removable $i$-nodes ordered top to bottom, and its reduced form, after deleting zero entries, $+^a-^b$ is well defined; the good $i$-node of $\lambda$ is the removable node of the first surviving $-$, the cogood $i$-node is the addable node of the last surviving $+$, and $\varepsilon_i(\lambda),\varphi_i(\lambda)$ are the numbers of surviving $-$ and $+$ signs ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

[F3] The reduction of a signature word is confluent, and the zero-suppressed normal form $+^a-^b$ can be computed by scanning the word from left to right, pushing each non-cancelled $-$ on a stack and letting each $+$ cancel the top $-$ of the stack if the stack is nonempty, and surviving otherwise; the surviving signs in their original order are exactly the normal form ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

affected_use.snippet:
Fix a finite integer $e \ge 2$ and charge $0$, with the independent-root affine
Cartan datum, its lattices and its diagram reflection $\tau$ fixed as in
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]: $I = \mathbb{Z}/e\mathbb{Z}$, simple
roots $\alpha_i$, fundamental weights $\Lambda_i$, $\delta$, and
$\tau(i) = -i$. A *node* is a pair $(r,c) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, and
the *residue* of a node is $\operatorname{res}(r,c) := c - r \bmod e$; this is
the level-one, charge-$0$ specialization of the residue used in
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]. We use the
English convention (rows increase downwards) and the node language of
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]] and
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]].

[F4] $F_{\mathrm{QG}}$ is a direct sum over all partitions with $\operatorname{wt}(|\lambda\rangle) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\lambda)\alpha_i$ and $\sum_i m_i(\lambda) = |\lambda|$ ([[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]]); the residue of a node is $c - r \bmod e$ and a partition is $e$-regular (resp. $e$-restricted) exactly as in the Definition ([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]], [[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

affected_use.snippet:
Work Brundan's Example 2.8 (complete 34-page author manuscript, p. 5) in his
conventions: $\lambda=(6,4,4,3,2)$, padded by $\lambda_6=0$ with $n=6$, is $\ell$-restricted for $\ell=3$ and
$\ell=4$, residues are $r-c\bmod\ell$ in the source's orientation (the
negative of the $c-r$ convention of this page,
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]),
$R(\lambda)=\{1,3,4,5\}$ is the set of removable rows, and for
$i\in R(\lambda)$ one compares $B_{i,6}(\lambda)\cap R(\lambda)$ with
$C_{i,6}(\lambda)\cap R(\lambda)$ in the lattice order $\downarrow$, where
$$B_{i,j}(\lambda)=\{k\in[i..j):\operatorname{res}_\ell(i,\lambda_i)= \operatorname{res}_\ell(k+1,\lambda_{k+1}+1)\},\qquad C_{i,j}(\lambda)=\{k\in(i..j):\operatorname{res}_\ell(i,\lambda_i)= \operatorname{res}_\ell(k,\lambda_k)\},$$
and $A\downarrow B$ means that there is an injection $\theta:A\to B$ with
$\theta(a)\le a$ for all $a$.

[F1] The source's definitions: $R(\lambda)=\{i:\lambda_i\ne\lambda_{i+1}\}$ is the set of removable rows, the node $(i,\lambda_i)$ has residue $i-\lambda_i\bmod\ell$, $R^{normal}(\lambda)=\{i\in R(\lambda):B_{i,n}(\lambda)\downarrow C_{i,n}(\lambda)\}$ with $n=6$, and $R^{good}(\lambda)=\{i\in R^{normal}(\lambda):$ no $j\in R^{normal}(\lambda)$ with $j<i$ and the same residue$\}$; there is at most one good row per residue (Brundan §2.2-2.4 and Remark 2.7, printed pp. 3-5). These are this page's normal and good nodes on the same partition, with residue names negated; Remark 2.4(II) instead compares Brundan's convention with Kleshchev's older convention on the transpose ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

affected_use.snippet: For every restricted $\lambda$ the nonzero $E_iD(\lambda)$ have simple socle and simple head $D(\widetilde e_i\lambda)$, each once, and $E_iD(\lambda)=0$ exactly when the good $i$-deletion is undefined. Similarly the nonzero $F_iD(\mu)$ have simple socle and simple head $D(\widetilde f_i\mu)$, each once, and vanish exactly when the cogood $i$-addition is undefined. Here signatures use content $c-r$, top-to-bottom order, cancellation of $-+$, first surviving minus and last surviving plus ([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). In particular the restriction socle is the multiplicity-free sum over good residues. This proves endpoints, not total composition multiplicities. Composite $e$, arbitrary characteristic, nonsquare $q$, and rank zero are included.

affected_use.snippet:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. Every $p$-restricted partition
$\mu$ of $d$ is obtained from the empty partition by $d$ successive cogood
additions: there are residues $i_1,\dots,i_d$ with
$$\mu=\tilde f_{i_d}\cdots\tilde f_{i_1}\varnothing;$$
equivalently, every $p$-restricted $\mu\ne\varnothing$ has at least one good
node, and successive good deletions carry $\mu$ to $\varnothing$
([[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]],
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Hence, in
the graph whose vertices are the $p$-restricted partitions and whose edges
join $\nu$ to $\tilde f_i\nu$ for every $i$ for which the operator is
defined, the empty partition is the unique vertex of rank $0$ and every
vertex is reached from it; dually every vertex reaches the empty partition by
successive good deletions. The argument is choice-free.

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$; let $A$ be the good
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\setminus A$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). For the
residue-summand functor $E_i$ of
[[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]] the
module $E_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to
$D(\nu)$, and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $E_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)$. Thus the Loewy endpoints are simple even though the
formal character of $E_iD(\mu)$ may contain the additional normal-node
factors of
[[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]].

[F6] The good $i$-node is the topmost normal $i$-node, so the normal
$i$-nodes weakly below it are exactly all normal $i$-nodes of $\mu$, and
there are $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$ of them
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]).

affected_use.snippet:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ (every field is splitting for
symmetric groups, so no algebraic closedness is needed) and let $\lambda$ be
a $p$-regular partition of $n$
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]), so that $D^\lambda$ is the
simple head of the Specht module $S^\lambda_k$
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]). Let
$A=(j,\lambda_j)$ be a removable node of $\lambda$ whose removal
$\lambda(j)$ is again $p$-regular, and call $A$ **normal** for $\lambda$ when
the transposed node $(\lambda_j,j)$ of the $p$-restricted partition
$\lambda'$ is a normal node in the sense of
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]] (this is
Kleshchev's normality; it is computed in the reduced signature of the correct
residue class of $\lambda'$). Then
$$[\,D^\lambda{\downarrow}_{S_{n-1}}:D^{\lambda(j)}\,]=0$$
if $A$ is not normal, and
$$[\,D^\lambda{\downarrow}_{S_{n-1}}:D^{\lambda(j)}\,]=1+\#\{B:\ B\ \text{is a normal removable node of }\lambda\text{ strictly above }A\text{ with }\operatorname{res}(B)=\operatorname{res}(A)\}$$
if $A$ is normal. Here $\operatorname{res}$ is the residue $c-r\bmod p$ and
"above" means strictly smaller row index. Equivalently, the multiplicity is the piecewise integer
$\gamma(A)=\mathbf1_{A\text{ normal}}\cdot\#\{B:B\text{ normal removable, weakly above }A,\ \operatorname{res}(B)=\operatorname{res}(A)\}$.
Thus $A$ is normal precisely when this piecewise multiplicity is nonzero.

[F4] The general cellular rank-one action gives simplicity, absolute simplicity and completeness of the actual nonzero Schur cell quotients ([[thm-nonzero-cell-heads-classify-the-simple-modules-of-a-cellular-algebra]]). The signature convention is [[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]], and restriction has its usual exact group-module meaning ([[def-restriction-induction-and-coinduction-for-group-modules]]).
